3-point ELR seat belts have been adopted for all seats.
For the front seats, seat belts with pretensioner and force limiter have been provided for both the driver and front passenger seats.

Adjustable shoulder belt anchors with 4-step vertical adjustment have been adopted for the driver and front passenger seat belts to accommodate occupants of various builds. In addition, the slip joint is built into the center pillar upper garnish for improved appearance.

A child seat fixing mechanism has been adopted for the rear 3-point ELR seat belts. The child seat fixing mechanism is activated by pulling the belt out fully; in this state the belt can be retracted but cannot be pulled out. When the belt is retracted beyond a certain amount, the child seat fixing mechanism is released and the belt returns to normal ELR state.

The inner buckles of the rear outboard seats are a self-standing type that protrudes from the seat surface, while the contact feel when moving across the seat has been reduced, achieving both ease of seat belt fastening and comfort.

The millimeter wave radar sensor assembly recognizes vehicles and obstacles in the vehicle's path, and the distance control computer assembly determines whether a collision is unavoidable from the position, speed and path of the object.

The distance control computer assembly sends that information via CAN communication to the ABS & traction actuator assembly (skid control computer) and the seat belt control computer, operating each control of the pre-crash safety system.

When the ABS & traction actuator assembly (skid control computer) recognizes emergency braking by the driver or determines that there is a high possibility that the vehicle will become uncontrollable (spinning, etc.), it sends that information to the seat belt control computer via CAN communication to operate the pre-crash seat belt.

ENTRY.PTXT: When the distance control computer (pre-crash safety computer) determines that a collision is unavoidable, the belt is retracted by the motor to increase the pretensioner effect.

When the skid control computer recognizes emergency braking by the driver or determines that there is a high possibility that the vehicle will become uncontrollable, the belt is retracted by the motor to increase the pretensioner effect.

When the distance control computer (pre-crash safety computer) determines that the possibility of a collision is high, brake hydraulic pressure is boosted to increase the braking effect when the brake pedal is depressed.

When the distance control computer (pre-crash safety computer) determines that there is a possibility of a collision, it warns the driver with a buzzer and display. Furthermore, when a collision is determined to be unavoidable, the brakes are applied to reduce speed even without brake operation by the driver.

ITEM.PTXT: The millimeter wave radar sensor assembly is mounted behind the radiator grille.
By turning the radar axis adjustment bolts and gear section, the radar axis can be adjusted within a range of 3° up, down, left and right.
Adjust the radar axis carefully using TaSCAN and a level.

MECA.TITLE: Detection Method for Relative Distance and Relative Speed

ITEM.PTXT: When an object exists within the range of the millimeter wave radar sensor assembly, the distance, relative speed and direction of the object are detected from the reflected waves, and based on that data the pre-crash safety computer determines whether a collision is unavoidable.

The direction of the object is detected from the angle of the reflected waves, the distance from the time between emitting the radio waves and the return of the reflected waves, and the speed of the object from the frequency change of the reflected waves (Doppler effect).
In addition, on curves, the radius of the curve is estimated based on information from the yaw rate sensor assembly and steering sensor, and the path is corrected.
